 Methyl acetate (also known as methyl ethanoate, acetic acid methyl ester, MeOAc, Tereton, Devoton) is a carboxylate ester with a molecular formula of C 3 H 6 O 2 . It is a clear, colourless liquid that has a typical ester odour similar to glues and nail polish removers. It is very flammable with a flashpoint of -10° C and a flammability rating of 3. Methyl acetate is commonly used in low toxicity solvents such as glues, nail polish removers.

 It is highly miscible with all common organic solvents (alcohols, ketones, glycols, esters) but has only slight miscibility in water, but becomes more soluble in water with elevated temperatures. It is commonly found in fruits such as apples, grapes and bananas.

## Is Propionic Acid a Solvent?

Yes. Propionic acid (C3H6O2, CAS 79-09-4) is a versatile organic acid that functions as a solvent in many industrial formulations. It is a colorless liquid with a sharp, slightly rancid odor, and it mixes completely with water and with most common organic solvents, including ethanol, ether, chloroform and acetone. This unusual combination of full water miscibility and good organic solvency comes from its short carbon chain carrying both a hydrophobic alkyl group and a hydrophilic carboxyl group. As a result, propionic acid can dissolve both polar and non-polar substances and acts as a coupling agent in complex formulations, helping incompatible phases stay mixed in industrial blending systems.
